'''''Brasenia''''' is a [[genus]] belonging to the family [[Cabombaceae]], consisting of one species, '''''Brasenia schreberi''''', commonly known as '''watershield'''. It is widely distributed in North America, the [[West Indies]], northern South America (Venezuela, Guyana), eastern Asia (China, Japan, Korea, [[Primorye]]), Australia, the [[Indian subcontinent]], and parts of Africa.<ref name=iu>{{cite web |url=https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:605270-1 |title=''Brasenia schreberi'' J.F.Gmel.|website=Plants of the World Online |publisher=Royal Botanics Gardens Kew}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://bonap.net/MapGallery/County/Brasenia%20schreberi.png |series=Biota of North America Program|title= 2013 county distribution map}}</ref><ref>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=104529 Flora of China Vol. 6 Page 119, {{lang|zh|莼菜属}} chun cai shu, ''Brasenia'' Schreber, Gen. Pl. 1: 372. 1789. ]</ref><ref>{{cite book|editor=Iwatsuki, K.|editor2= Boufford, D.E. |editor3= Ohba, H. |year=2006|title= Flora of Japan |volume=IIa|publisher= Kodansha Ltd.|location= Tokyo}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |editor-last1=Hokche |editor-first1=Omaira |editor-last2=Berry |editor-first2=Paul E. |editor-last3=Huber |editor-first3=Otto |title=Nuevo catálogo de la flora vascular de Venezuela |date=2008 |publisher=Fundación Instituto Botánico de Venezuela Dr. Tobías Lasser |location=Caracas, Venezuela |isbn=978-980-6355-07-1 |pages=1–859 |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/319162740}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last1=Figueiredo, E. |last2=Smith, G.F. |year=2008 |title=Plants of Angola |url=https://www.sanbi.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/2008_Strelitzia22.pdf |series=Strelitzia |volume=22 |pages=1–279 |publisher=South African National Botanical Institute |location=Pretoria}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1=Acevedo-Rodríguez | first1=Pedro | last2=Strong | first2=Mark T. | title=Catalogue of Seed Plants of the West Indies |url=https://botanicodesantiago.com/wp-content/uploads/2018/12/Catalogue-of-Seed-Plants-of-the-West-Indies-Pedro-Acevedo-Rodriguez.pdf| journal=Smithsonian Contributions to Botany | date=2012 | volume=98 | pages=1–1192 | doi=10.5479/si.0081024X.98.1 }}</ref>
[[File:Junsai-asaproductinastore-march16-2014.jpg|thumb|For sale in a [[Japan]]ese supermarket, 2014]]

''Brasenia'' is a perennial [[aquatic plant]] with floating, [[peltate]] leaves and [[rhizomatous]] stems.  It is identified by its bright green leaves, small purple flowers that bloom from June through September, and a thick [[mucilage]] that covers all of the underwater organs, including the underside of the leaves, stems, and developing buds. This mucilage may be an anti-herbivore defence trait,<ref>{{cite book|author=Keddy, P.A. |year=2010|title= Wetland Ecology: Principles and Conservation |edition=2nd |publisher= Cambridge University Press|location= Cambridge, UK|pages= Figure 6.9}}</ref> perhaps to deter snail grazing. It grows in shallow water of lakes, rivers and beaver ponds, particularly those with somewhat acidic water.

[[File:Junsai held above Soup.jpg|thumb|Junsai with visible mucilage.]]

== Characteristics ==
[[File:Ponds along Attikamek Trail at Sault Ste. Marie Canal NHS.JPG|thumb|Ponds along Attikamek Trail at [[Sault Ste. Marie Canal]]]]
''Brasenia'' exhibits [[anemophily|wind pollination]].  The flowers have a two-day blooming period. On the first day, the functionally female, or pistillate flower, extends above the surface of the water and exposes the receptive stigmas. The flower then recedes below the water surface and on the following day emerges as a functionally male, or staminate flower.  It is elevated higher than on the previous day and the anther-bearing filaments are extended beyond the female carpels.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Taylor | first1=Mackenzie L. | last2=Osborn | first2=Jeffrey M. | title=Pollen ontogeny in ''Brasenia'' (Cabombaceae, Nymphaeales) | journal=American Journal of Botany | date=2006 | volume=93 | issue=3 | pages=344–356 | doi=10.3732/ajb.93.3.344 |doi-access=free | pmid=21646195 | bibcode=2006AmJB...93..344T }}</ref> The anthers dehisce, releasing the pollen, and the flower is then withdrawn below the water where the fruit develops.

==Cytology==
The [[chloroplast genome]] is 158951 base pairs (bp) long.<ref name = "Gruenstaeudl et al., 2017">{{cite journal |last1=Gruenstaeudl |first1=Michael |last2=Nauheimer |first2=Lars |last3=Borsch |first3=Thomas |title=Plastid genome structure and phylogenomics of Nymphaeales: Conserved gene order and new insights into relationships |journal=Plant Systematics and Evolution |date=2017 |volume=303 |issue=9 |pages=1251–1270 |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/318253682 |doi=10.1007/s00606-017-1436-5 |bibcode=2017PSyEv.303.1251G }}</ref> The [[mitochondrial genome]] is composed of six parts ranging from 110220 bp to 628257 bp in size. The complete mitogenome is 1.49 mega–base-pair ([[Base_pair#Length_measurements|Mb]]) long.<ref name = "Shan et al., 2014">{{cite journal |last1=Shan |first1=Yuanyu |last2=Li |first2=Jingling |last3=Duan |first3=Xinmei |last4=Zhang |first4=Xue |last5=Yu |first5=Jie |title=Elucidating the multichromosomal structure within the ''Brasenia schreberi'' mitochondrial genome through assembly and analysis |journal=BMC Genomics |date=2024 |volume=25 |issue=1 |article-number=422 |doi=10.1186/s12864-024-10331-0 |doi-access=free |pmid=38684976 |pmc=11059650 }}</ref> The [[nuclear genome]] is 1170.4 Mb long.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Lu |first1=Bei |last2=Shi |first2=Tao |last3=Chen |first3=Jinming |title=Chromosome-level genome assembly of watershield (''Brasenia schreberi'') |journal=Scientific Data |date=2023 |volume=10 |issue=1 |article-number=467 |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/s41597-023-02380-z.pdf |doi=10.1038/s41597-023-02380-z |pmid=37468511 |pmc=10356934 |bibcode=2023NatSD..10..467L }}</ref>

== Uses ==
''Brasenia'' is cultivated as a vegetable in China (where it is known as ''chúncài'' {{lang|zh|{{linktext|莼菜}}}}) and where it is used in [[Hangzhou]] in the well-known local speciality "West Lake Water Shield Soup"<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gotohz.com/hzlywywb/whatishot/bestofhangzhou/201307/t20130718_86681.shtml|title=Hangzhou Cuisine|access-date=22 April 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140821112832/http://www.gotohz.com/hzlywywb/whatishot/bestofhangzhou/201307/t20130718_86681.shtml|archive-date=2014-08-21|url-status=dead}}</ref> and in Japan.

The mucilage it produces has been found to have anti-algal and anti-bacterial properties that may be useful as a natural weed control.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Elakovich|first1=Stella D.|last2=Wooten|first2=Jean W. |date=September 1987|title=An examination of the phytotoxicity of the water shield, ''Brasenia schreberi'' |journal=Journal of Chemical Ecology|language=en|volume=13|issue=9|pages=1935–1940|doi=10.1007/BF01014676|pmid=24302458 |bibcode=1987JCEco..13.1935E |s2cid=37729620 }}</ref>

== History ==
Species of ''Brasenia'' occurred during the interglacial of Europe, but like many other aquatic plant species and genera, it does not occur there now.<ref>{{cite book|author=Sculthorpe, C. D. |year=1967|title= The Biology of Aquatic Vascular Plants|edition= Reprinted 1985 |publisher=Edward Arnold|location= London |page= 404}}</ref>

== Name ==
''Brasenia schreberi'' has the common name watershield.<ref name = "NatureServe" />

The genus may commemorate the surgeon and [[Moravian Church|Moravian]] missionary [[Christoph Brasen]] (1738-1774), who was the first superintendent of the Moravian mission at [[Nain, Newfoundland and Labrador|Nain]] in [[Labrador]].<ref>{{cite journal|author=Pringle, James S. |title=Possible eponymy of the generic name ''Brasenia'' Schreb. |journal= Sida |volume= 16|issue= 3 |pages= 597–600|year= 1995 |url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/34587#page/602/mode/1up}}</ref>

==Conservation==
It is classified as least concern (LC) by The [[IUCN]] Red List.<ref name = "Maiz-Tome, 2016" /> It is classified as vulnerable (VU) in South Korea.<ref name = "Kim, 2014">{{cite web|editor=Kim, S. B. |year=2014 |url=http://archive.nationalredlist.org/files/2016/04/Korean-Red-List-of-Threatened-Species-English-compressed-2.pdf |title=Korean red list of threatened species|publisher= National Institute of Biological Resources}}</ref> The [[NatureServe conservation status]] is G5 Secure.<ref name = "NatureServe" /> Under the [[Flora and Fauna Guarantee Act 1988]], it is categorised as Critically Endangered (CR).<ref name = "VicFlora">{{cite web|publisher=Royal Botanic Gardens Victoria|title= ''Brasenia schreberi'' J.F.Gmel. |website=VicFlora Flora of Victoria|access-date= December 7, 2024|url= https://vicflora.rbg.vic.gov.au/flora/taxon/6d16f9c6-4db0-42a7-a4ab-595ec6116c4e}}</ref>
